= Description Lists

A term and what it means, separated by a double colon:

term:: The definition, on the same line.
another term:: Terms may hold spaces, so a phrase works as well as a word.

The delimiter is the first `::` with a space after it, which is why a term
may itself contain colons:

`:date:`:: An attribute name, colons and all, read as it was written.
`_media/`:: A directory whose name begins with an underscore.

A definition may carry inline formatting, and may soft-wrap the way a list
item does:

soft-wrapped:: This definition runs onto a second line, indented under the
  term the way prose usually is, and the indentation is presentation rather
  than content.
formatted:: Definitions hold *bold*, _italic_, `monospace`, and
  link:https://example.org/[links] like anything else.

A term may be defined on the line below rather than beside it:

standalone::
  The definition begins here.

Because the delimiter needs a following space, a block image is unambiguous
and needs no ordering rule to stay one:

image::diagram.png[A diagram]
